# WAS_mme_CCA { #wass2s.WAS_mme_CCA }

```python
WAS_mme_CCA(
    n_modes=4,
    n_pca_modes=8,
    standardize=False,
    use_coslat=True,
    use_pca=True,
    combine='mean',
    detrend=True,
    dist_method='nonparam',
    positive_support=True,
)
```

Canonical Correlation Analysis MME.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name        | Type                | Description                                                                                                                                                                          | Default      |
|-------------|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|
| n_modes     | int                 | Number of canonical modes for xeofs.cross.CCA (default 4).                                                                                                                           | `4`          |
| n_pca_modes | int                 | PCA modes kept before CCA when ``use_pca`` is True (default 8).                                                                                                                      | `8`          |
| standardize | bool                | Passed to xeofs.cross.CCA. Keep False; the framework already standardizes (default False).                                                                                           | `False`      |
| use_coslat  | bool                | Cosine-latitude weighting inside the CCA (default True).                                                                                                                             | `True`       |
| use_pca     | bool                | Pre-filter each field with PCA before the CCA (default True).                                                                                                                        | `True`       |
| combine     | (mean, meof)        | How the M models enter the CCA predictor field.                                                                                                                                      | `'mean'`     |
| detrend     | bool                | Apply ``detrended_data`` to both predictor and predictand in ``forecast``, exactly like ``WAS_CCA_op`` does unconditionally (default True). Set False only for ablation comparisons. | `True`       |
| dist_method | (nonparam, bestfit) | Tercile-probability strategy (default 'nonparam').                                                                                                                                   | `'nonparam'` |

## Methods

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [compute_model](#wass2s.WAS_mme_CCA.compute_model) | Deterministic CCA hindcast for one CV fold, in the standardized space |
| [forecast](#wass2s.WAS_mme_CCA.forecast) | Operational CCA forecast for a single target year. |

### compute_model { #wass2s.WAS_mme_CCA.compute_model }

```python
WAS_mme_CCA.compute_model(X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test=None, **kwargs)
```

Deterministic CCA hindcast for one CV fold, in the standardized space
the framework hands in. No detrend here — matches WAS_CCA_op.compute_model
which is also detrend-free. The same_kind_model2 branch reverse-standardizes
the output afterwards.

### forecast { #wass2s.WAS_mme_CCA.forecast }

```python
WAS_mme_CCA.forecast(
    Predictant,
    clim_year_start,
    clim_year_end,
    Predictor,
    hindcast_det,
    Predictor_for_year,
    best_code_da=None,
    best_shape_da=None,
    best_loc_da=None,
    best_scale_da=None,
)
```

Operational CCA forecast for a single target year.

  predictor →  standardize  →  detrended_data()                 (raw, not pre-standardized)
  predictand →  standardize  →  detrended_data() (always unconditional)
  forecast-year predictor  →  apply_detrend_data()
  fit CCA on (predictor_dt, predictand_st_dt)
  result  →  + apply_detrend_data()  →  reverse_standardize()
